headline: Law extends through 2028 the Secret Service's ability to pay protective staff overtime above normal federal pay caps, and adds reporting to Congress.
what_it_does: The law lets the U.S. Secret Service keep paying protective services employees overtime and other premium pay above the usual federal limits through 2028, applied retroactively to December 31, 2023. Employees who do routine administrative or technical work cannot get this extra pay. The Secret Service must report to Congress on staffing demand, ways to cut overtime, and detailed data on who received pay above the cap.

who_it_affects.how: They can continue to receive overtime and premium pay above the normal federal cap through 2028.

who_it_affects.group: Secret Service employees doing routine administrative or technical work
who_it_affects.how: They are not eligible for premium pay above the cap under this law.
The agency must send Congress a report within 180 days on protection staffing and reducing overtime, plus yearly pay data updated every quarter.
Lawmakers will receive regular data on above-cap pay, unpaid amounts due to the cap, and employees who left after receiving such pay.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted February 6, 2024; the pay extension applies as if enacted December 31, 2023, and runs through 2028. The first staffing report is due within 180 days of enactment.
